title: Advice time yields polynomial-size circuits
statement: Let $c,C,d$ be natural numbers and let $a:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ satisfy $a(n)\le C(n+1)^d$ for every $n$. If a language $L$ has advice of length exactly $a(n)$ and is decidable, on every input paired with its advice, by a finite Turing machine within a constant multiple of $n^c+1$ steps, then $L$ has a family of Boolean circuits with fan-in at most two and size bounded by a polynomial in the input length.
hypotheses_covered: $L$ is decidable with advice of length exactly $a(n)$ in time a constant multiple of $n^c+1$
